# Persistent indexed history

A successor index describes each cons cell. The double-line constructor rule supports both construction and pattern decomposition; operation bodies are checked against it, rather than postulated. Indices establish shape under these open datatype rules, not purity or universal behavioral laws.

```shen
(datatype history
  ___________________
  [] : (history A 0);
  X : A; S : (history A N);
  =================================
  [X | S] : (history A [succ N]);)

(define h-empty {--> (history A 0)} -> [])
(define h-append {A --> (history A N) --> (history A [succ N])} X S -> [X | S])
(define h-newest {(history A [succ N]) --> A} [X | _] -> X)
(define h-remove {(history A [succ N]) --> (history A N)} [_ | S] -> S)
(define h-double {(history number [succ N]) --> (history number [succ N])}
  [X | S] -> [(* X 2) | S])
(define h-test {string --> boolean --> boolean}
  _ true -> true
  Label false -> (simple-error Label))
(h-test "persistence and predecessor" 
  (= (let S (h-append 7 (h-append 3 (h-empty)))
          D (h-double S)
       [(h-newest S) (h-newest D) (h-newest (h-remove D)) (h-newest (h-remove S))])
     [7 14 3 3]))
```

<!-- reject: h-bad-growth -->
```shen
(define h-bad-growth {A --> (history A N) --> (history A [succ N])}
  _ S -> S)
```

<!-- reject: h-read-empty -->
```shen
(define h-read-empty {--> number} -> (h-newest (h-empty)))
```

<!-- reject: h-read-removed -->
```shen
(define h-read-removed {--> number} -> (h-newest (h-remove (h-append 1 (h-empty)))))
```

# Review of the claimed stack proof

The claim is false. The operation rules are trusted axioms over untyped closures: client checking proves consequences of those rules, not that the implementation satisfies them. Smallest counterexample: `top(push(1, empty))` typechecks as a number under the claimed rules, but push returns `empty`, so it cannot deliver 1; depending on the empty closure, it fails or returns some unrelated value. No execution result is asserted here.

Repair push to construct a fresh persistent node containing the new value and predecessor. Prefer a concrete indexed representation with constructor introduction/elimination rules and typecheck empty, push, top, and pop bodies, including a rejected growth body returning its input. Alternatively, audit an untyped representation and explicitly mark operation rules as trusted. In either case test and reason about `top(push(x,s)) = x` and `pop(push(x,s)) = s`, old aliases, and multi-element order. Structural indices constrain admissible length shapes, not ordering or those equations. Persistence and purity require analysis of mutation, aliasing and captured values; termination requires a separate argument. Tests give examples, not universal proofs. All judgments remain relative to the active datatype axioms and runtime.

# Cyclic prerequisites

A finite functional graph and a visited worklist avoid Prolog's depth-first cycle hazard. The input is a ground job symbol; unknown symbols have no outgoing edges. `element?` is ordinary ground membership, not negation-as-failure. Each first visit expands its outgoing edges once; origin starts visited, so it is excluded even on a cycle. Returned order is traversal order, not a specification.

```shen
(define edges {symbol --> (list symbol)}
 seed -> [package]
 compile -> [seed]
 package -> [compile]
 publish -> [package]
 _ -> [])
(define walk {(list symbol) --> (list symbol) --> (list symbol)}
 [] Seen -> Seen
 [X | Xs] Seen -> (walk Xs Seen) where (element? X Seen)
 [X | Xs] Seen -> (walk (append (edges X) Xs) [X | Seen]))
(define requirements {symbol --> (list symbol)}
 J -> (remove J (walk (edges J) [J])))
(define qcheck {string --> boolean --> boolean}
 _ true -> true
 L false -> (simple-error L))
(qcheck "publish" (= (requirements publish) [seed compile package]))
(qcheck "seed cycle" (= (requirements seed) [compile package]))
(qcheck "docs" (= (requirements docs) []))
```

Completeness follows by induction on paths: every newly reached vertex is expanded, while already expanded vertices need not be expanded again. Finite reachable vertices and finite edge lists ensure termination here. These facts depend on the closed edge definition and ground finite inputs; the arrow type itself does not establish them.

# Vocabulary-driven phrases

The vocabulary is data, not a table of answers. The generator takes its color list as an argument so extension changes only the source supplied to it. Empty strings represent epsilon; joining handles either side without introducing spaces.

```shen
(define v-join {string --> string --> string}
 "" Y -> Y
 X "" -> X
 X Y -> (cn X (cn " " Y)))
(define v-row {string --> (list string) --> (list string)}
 _ [] -> []
 C [O | Os] -> [(v-join C O) | (v-row C Os)])
(define phrases {(list string) --> (list string) --> (list string)}
 [] _ -> []
 [C | Cs] Os -> (append (v-row C Os) (phrases Cs Os)))
(define v-colors {--> (list string)} -> ["amber" "violet"])
(define v-extended {--> (list string)} -> (append (v-colors) ["teal"]))
(define v-objects {--> (list string)} -> ["kite" "cup"])
(define unique? {(list string) --> boolean}
 [] -> true
 [X | Xs] -> (and (not (element? X Xs)) (unique? Xs)))
(define vcheck {string --> boolean --> boolean}
 _ true -> true
 L false -> (simple-error L))
(vcheck "four" (= (phrases (v-colors) (v-objects)) ["amber kite" "amber cup" "violet kite" "violet cup"]))
(vcheck "six" (= (phrases (v-extended) (v-objects)) ["amber kite" "amber cup" "violet kite" "violet cup" "teal kite" "teal cup"]))
(vcheck "unique" (and (unique? (phrases (v-colors) (v-objects))) (unique? (phrases (v-extended) (v-objects)))))
(vcheck "epsilon" (= (phrases ["" "amber"] ["" "cup"]) ["" "cup" "amber" "amber cup"]))
```

Each color generates one row over all objects; concatenating all rows gives the Cartesian product, so every pair occurs exactly once if the input lists have unique entries. Rendered strings are unique only if distinct pairs render distinctly, which is true for these words but not arbitrary strings or epsilon-containing vocabularies. The explicit uniqueness checks cover the two supplied vocabularies.

# Explicit account transition and private counter

The fee is captured at configuration time, while balance and action are explicit inputs. The example assumes nonnegative balances, amounts, and fees; these constraints are not enforced by the types. `insufficient` is an explicit result and no balance is mutated.

```shen
(datatype action
 N : number; ================= [credit N] : action;
 N : number; ================= [debit N] : action;)
(datatype outcome
 N : number; ================= [balance N] : outcome;
 _____________________________ insufficient : outcome;)
(define account-step {number --> number --> action --> outcome}
 _ B [credit N] -> [balance (+ B N)]
 Fee B [debit N] -> insufficient where (< B (+ N Fee))
 Fee B [debit N] -> [balance (- B (+ N Fee))])
(define account {number --> (number --> action --> outcome)}
 Fee -> (account-step Fee))
(define tcheck {string --> boolean --> boolean}
 _ true -> true
 L false -> (simple-error L))
(tcheck "configuration and replay"
 (= (let A (account 1) B (account 3) Old 10
      [(A Old [debit 4]) (B Old [debit 4]) (A Old [debit 4]) [balance Old] (A Old [credit 2]) (A Old [debit 10])])
    [[balance 5] [balance 3] [balance 5] [balance 10] [balance 12] insufficient]))

(define ctr-dispatch {(vector number) --> symbol --> number}
 Cell peek -> (<-vector Cell 1)
 Cell inc -> (let N (+ (<-vector Cell 1) 1) W (vector-> Cell 1 N) N)
 _ _ -> (simple-error "unknown counter command"))
(define counter {number --> (symbol --> number)}
 Start -> (let Cell (vector 1) W (vector-> Cell 1 Start) (ctr-dispatch Cell)))
(tcheck "alias and separate factories"
 (= (let C (counter 0) Alias C D (counter 0) First (C inc)
       [(Alias peek) (D peek) (Alias inc) (C peek)])
    [1 0 2 2]))
```

The counter owns a fresh vector per factory invocation; its aliases share it. This is behavioral reasoning about these bodies and runtime allocation, not an arrow-type guarantee of freshness, purity, replay or command protocol. The transition similarly relies on the given arithmetic and immutable numeric policy, not a type-level effect system.

# Trial report

Command actually run from the trial directory:

```sh
ls input-skills; find input-skills -type f; echo "$BIFROST_TRIAL_BIN"
$BIFROST_TRIAL_BIN skills check --impl shen-jit --dir answers
```

The checker reported **8 blocks, 0 failed (shen-jit)**. It checked each executable fence in a fresh process with the earlier accepted fences in its file; the review is prose and has no executable fence. No dependencies were installed or runtime/checker changed. There were no failed checker attempts.

- **vocabulary — complete for the stated examples.** Typed Cartesian-product generator over source lists, with epsilon-aware rendering. Exact four and six result lists, uniqueness, and epsilon cases are asserted. Completeness depends on finite source lists; output uniqueness additionally depends on injective rendering for the vocabulary. No trusted declarations or untyped boundaries.
- **history — complete for the requested interface.** Checked cons-based indexed representation and operation bodies, including a length-preserving numeric double. The test observes the old newest value, replacement, and both predecessors. The checker rejected the named false-growth implementation and the two empty-read clients. Concrete datatype rules are part of the trusted type theory; no unchecked operation declarations. This is not a formal proof of all semantic laws or purity.
- **prerequisites — complete for the ground finite graph.** A typed visited worklist expands each discovered job, with the starting job previsited. Tests assert exact results for publish, seed, and isolated docs. Ground membership, not Prolog negation, controls revisits. Termination and completeness are argued from this finite graph, not established by types. No declarations or untyped boundaries.
- **parser — complete for the requested flat token language.** Typed Shen-YACC semantic actions construct an AST with left-folding tails and precedence, then a checked evaluator computes its value. Tests cover precedence, repeated operators and exact associativity, empty and missing-operand input, and trailing tokens. The `number?` verified bridge and conditional refinement are trusted datatype rules; no untyped parse-result declaration. The typechecker does not prove grammar completeness, termination, lexer behavior, or general semantic equivalence; tests are finite.
- **transition — complete for the specified behaviors under documented nonnegative input assumptions.** A configured closure captures the fee, with explicit balance/action and tagged result; a separate closure captures a freshly allocated mutable vector. Assertions cover configurations, replay, unchanged input, credit, overdraft, aliases and distinct factories. The nonnegative domain is an assumption, not enforced. No declarations or untyped boundaries. Effects, freshness and replay are behavioral claims about bodies/runtime, not arrow-type guarantees.
- **review — complete as a prose review.** The minimal typed client exposes the unjustified push axiom without inventing a runtime result. Repair and evidence strategy distinguish checked bodies, trusted rules and semantic properties. No executable claims or trusted declarations.
